TicketBunker / product exercise / 6 September 2026

Two users. One Bunker.

The work loop holds together. Protecting unsaved work and recovering from partial failures need attention.

Alice and Bob · separate clones and databases · 30 dummy tickets · 22 scenarios · 26 screenshots

Priority fixesAll scenariosScreenshotsTest limits

Fix these first

Fix first

Unsaved edits disappear

Edit a file, return to the ticket, then reopen it. The code draft is gone without a warning. Reproduced twice.

Next: Preserve the draft or ask before discarding it.

See screenshot 16 →

Fix first

Default ticket type fails after checkout

A ticket with no explicit type creates a Git branch, then fails intake. The user gets a diagnostic path, not a recovery action.

Next: Validate and normalize the ticket before changing the checkout.

See screenshot 25 →

Recovery

A real branch disappears from the workflow

After Bob’s branch creation fails to complete, the screen shows no branches. Retry says to choose the branch from that empty list.

Next: Refresh local branch state on failure and offer a way to finish linking it.

See screenshot 14 →

Visibility

Checks run, but their result is hard to see

The real test failed, then passed after the fix. The ticket shows the configured command, but not a separate pass/fail result.

Next: Show the observed result independently of the generated report.

See screenshot 13 →

Browser

Connect can silently do nothing

Repository connection depends on a native folder picker. The browser version gives no explanation when that picker is unavailable.

Next: Provide a browser-supported path input or clearly explain the requirement.

See screenshot 3 →

What worked

Creating and sharing a Bunker, inviting a second user, read-only member configuration, filters and pagination, saving code, protecting dirty worktrees, detecting newer commits, and reading another user’s report.

The configured test ran and failed on the deliberate defect. After a fix, commit and resynthesis, it passed. Cached tickets remained readable during a service outage, and synchronization recovered after restart.

What this does not prove

This is the captured September 6 source-build audit, not a new run or a statement that the findings remain unfixed. The real application interface, workers, database sharing and Git operations were exercised. Initial tickets were seeded through typed commands.

Agent reports used a deterministic stub. The native folder picker’s returned path was explicitly substituted after documenting its browser failure. Model reasoning, provider login, installed Windows/macOS builds, real network SSH authentication, Jira and full accessibility compliance were not tested.

Git commit and push were performed outside TicketBunker. All projects and people were dummy data. Coal was untouched. The lab services were stopped after capture. No production fixes were part of this audit.

Offline report. No external fonts, scripts, trackers or network requests.
